197	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
198	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
199	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
200	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
201	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
202	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
203	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
204	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
205	    case "$v" in
206	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
207	        *) return 1 ;;
208	    esac
209	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
210	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
211	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
212	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
213	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
214	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
215	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
216	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
217	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
218	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
219	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
220	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
221	    _runner_ended=true
222	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
223	    return 0
224	}

227	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
228	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
229	_runner_note_push_failure() {
230	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
231	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
232	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
233	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
234	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
235	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"

238	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
239	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
240	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
241	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
242	# when HEAD carries commits past the commit the run started from, which the
243	# engine sets before any stage (#2367; #1801 run 38290215955: the end of hydrate
244	# force-pushed main over the branch's earlier work). Advisory: a failure is
245	# reported, never fatal.
246	_runner_push_work_branch() {
247	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
248	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
249	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
250	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
251	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
252	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
253	    local _base="${ZBUILD_RUN_START_COMMIT:-}" _ahead
254	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
255	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
256	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
257	    local _err
258	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
259	        return 0
260	    fi
261	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
262	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
263	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
264	    return 0
265	}

267	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
268	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
269	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
270	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
271	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
272	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
273	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
274	    local _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch="${ZBUILD_RUN_BRANCH:-}"
275	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
276	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
277	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
278	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
279	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
280	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
281	        reattached)
282	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
283	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
284	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
285	        diverged)
286	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
287	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
288	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
289	    esac
290	    return 0
291	}

293	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
294	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
295	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
296	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
297	# never blocks a run.
298	#
299	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
300	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
301	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
302	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
303	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
304	# item 1 of #1807.
305	#
306	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
307	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
308	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
309	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
310	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
311	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
312	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
313	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
314	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
315	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
316	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
317	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
318	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
319	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
320	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
321	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
322	    # push had nothing to send.
323	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
324	
325	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
326	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
327	        saved)
328	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
329	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
330	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
331	            ;;
332	        failed)
333	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
334	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
335	            # no channel to surface on.
336	            #
337	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
338	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
339	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
340	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
341	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
342	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
343	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
344	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
345	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
346	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
347	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
348	            fi
349	            ;;
350	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
351	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
352	        *) : ;;
353	    esac
354	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
355	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
356	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
357	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
358	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
359	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
360	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
361	    local _leak=""
362	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
363	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
364	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
365	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
366	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
367	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
368	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
369	        return 0
370	    fi
371	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
372	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
373	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
374	    fi
375	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
376	    return 0
377	}

380	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
381	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
382	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
383	declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()

385	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
386	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
387	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
388	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
389	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
390	_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""

392	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
393	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
394	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
395	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
396	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
397	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
398	_runner_now_ms() {
399	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
400	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
401	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
402	        return 0
403	    fi
404	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
405	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
406	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
407	        return 0
408	    fi
409	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
410	}

412	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
413	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
414	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
415	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
416	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
417	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
418	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
419	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
420	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
421	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
422	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
423	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
424	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
425	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
426	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
427	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
428	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
429	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
430	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
431	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
432	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
433	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
434	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
435	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
436	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
437	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
438	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
439	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
440	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
441	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
442	    return 0
443	}

445	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
446	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
447	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
448	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
449	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
450	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
451	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
452	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
453	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
454	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
455	        local i
456	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
457	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
458	            sleep 0.1
459	        done
460	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
461	    fi
462	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
463	    return 0
464	}

466	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
467	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
468	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
469	_runner_now_short() {
470	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
471	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
472	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
473	        return 0
474	    fi
475	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
476	    local out
477	    # The shell's clock, in UTC (ADR-065 §5); the date forms stay as the fallback.
478	    TZ=UTC printf -v out '%(%H:%M:%S UTC)T' "$sec" 2>/dev/null && [[ -n "$out" ]] && { printf '%s' "$out"; return 0; }
479	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
480	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
481	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
482	    printf '%s' "$out"
483	}

485	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
486	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
487	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
488	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
489	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
490	_runner_duration_token() {
491	    local stage="$1"
492	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
493	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
494	        printf '?s'
495	        return 0
496	    fi
497	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
498	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
499	        printf '?s'
500	        return 0
501	    fi
502	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
503	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
504	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
505	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
506	    else
507	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
508	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
509	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
510	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
511	    fi
512	}

514	# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
515	# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
516	# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
517	# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
518	# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
519	_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
520	    local state_dir="$1"
521	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
522	    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
523	    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
524	    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
525	        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
526	    fi
527	    # #1874: the shape floor is part of the scope — computed here, mechanically,
528	    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
529	    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
530	    if [[ -n "$csv" && "$csv" != "${_RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY:-}" ]]; then
531	        _RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY="$csv"; _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV="$csv"
532	        if ! declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
533	            # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/shape-floor.sh
534	            source "${_ZBUILD_CONTRACT_LIB_DIR:-$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib}/shape-floor.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
535	        fi
536	        if declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
537	            local -a _scope_arr=() ; local _ff
538	            IFS=',' read -r -a _scope_arr <<< "$csv"
539	            while IFS= read -r _ff; do
540	                [[ -n "$_ff" && ",$_RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV," != *",$_ff,"* ]] && _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV+=",$_ff"
541	            done < <(sf_scope_floor_files "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-$PWD}" "${_scope_arr[@]}" 2>/dev/null)

548	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
549	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
550	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
551	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
552	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
553	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
554	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
555	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
556	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
557	_runner_record_report() {
558	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
559	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
560	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
561	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
562	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
563	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
564	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
565	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
566	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
567	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
568	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
569	        sleep 0.05
570	    done
571	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
572	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
573	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
574	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
575	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
576	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
577	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
578	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
579	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
580	    else
581	        rm -f "$tmp"
582	    fi
583	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
584	    return 0
585	}

587	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
588	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
589	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
590	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
591	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
592	#
593	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
594	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
595	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
596	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
597	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
598	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
599	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
600	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
601	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
602	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
603	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
604	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
605	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
606	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
607	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
608	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
609	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
610	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
611	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
612	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
613	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
614	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
615	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
616	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
617	        return 1
618	    fi
619	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
620	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
621	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
622	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
623	        return 1
624	    fi
625	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
626	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
627	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
628	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
629	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
630	    #
631	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
632	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
633	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
634	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
635	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
636	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
637	    #
638	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
639	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
640	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
641	    #
642	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
643	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
644	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
645	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
646	    fi
647	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
648	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
649	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
650	    # an unchanged tree.
651	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
652	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
653	    fi
654	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
655	    local _leaf _ok=1
656	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
657	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
658	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
659	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
660	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
661	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
662	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
663	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
664	        esac
665	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
666	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
667	            _ok=0
668	        fi
669	    done
670	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
671	}

673	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
674	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
675	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
676	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
677	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
678	#
679	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
680	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
681	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
682	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
683	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
684	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
685	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
686	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
687	#
688	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
689	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
690	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
691	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
692	#
693	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
694	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
695	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
696	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
697	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
698	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
699	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
700	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
701	_runner_template_personas() {
702	    awk '
703	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
704	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
705	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
706	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
707	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
708	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
709	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
710	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
711	        }
712	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
713	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
714	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
715	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
716	        }
717	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
718	}

720	# shellcheck disable=SC2120  # $1 is used by unit tests; runtime call sites pass no arg
721	_runner_validate_startup_preflight() {
722	    local _violation_fixture="${1:-}"
723	    local mode="${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-warn}"
724	    case "$mode" in
725	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
726	        *) mode="warn" ;;
727	    esac
728	
729	    # off = complete no-op, no output
730	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
731	
732	    local -a violations=()
733	    local fail_count=0
734	
735	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.
736	    if [[ -n "$_violation_fixture" ]]; then
737	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")
738	        fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
739	    fi
740	
741	    # ADR-051 §2 (amended 2026-10-12): every persona the template names — a
742	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
743	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
744	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.
745	    local _persona_missing=0 _pw _pid _pdir
746	    if [[ -n "${_TPL_SOURCE_FILE:-}" && -f "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE" ]]; then
747	        # shellcheck source=/dev/null  # followed, it re-reads runner.sh's own includes
748	        declare -F persona_find_dir >/dev/null 2>&1 \
749	            || source "$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/persona-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
750	        while IFS='|' read -r _pw _pid; do
751	            [[ -n "$_pid" ]] || continue
752	            _pdir="$(persona_find_dir "$_pid" 2>/dev/null)" && [[ -n "$_pdir" ]] && continue
753	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")
754	            fail_count=$((fail_count + 1)); _persona_missing=1
755	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")
756	    fi
757	
758	    # No violations → clean
759	    [[ $fail_count -eq 0 ]] && return 0
760	
761	    # Render all violations in a single block (render-all-at-once pattern).
762	    # #1826 moved the loop itself into _inputs_render_violations so the
763	    # pre-dispatch input presence check reuses it instead of being a third
764	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
765	    _inputs_render_violations \
766	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
767	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
768	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
769	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
770	        "${violations[@]}"
771	
772	    # Emit event (best-effort)
773	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
774	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
775	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
776	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
777	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true
778	    fi
779	
780	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
781	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
782	        return 0
783	    fi
784	
785	    # enforce: fail-closed
786	    return 1
787	}

812	# ─── _runner_pipeline_duration_token (#525) ──────────────────────────────────
813	# Parallel to _runner_duration_token but for the pipeline-wide window. No stage
814	# argument — reads _RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS directly. Returns "?s" on cache

817	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"

819	        printf '?s'
820	        return 0

824	        printf '?s'

826	    fi

828	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
829	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
830	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
831	    else
832	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
833	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
834	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
835	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"

858	        preflight_failed)                        verdict_glyph "warn" ;;

877	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
878	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
879	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
880	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
881	#
882	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
883	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
884	#
885	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
886	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
887	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
888	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
889	#
890	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
891	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
892	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
893	# against banner-write failures.
894	# _runner_restore_stderr — point fd 2 back at the runner's own stderr, saved at
895	# startup in _RUNNER_ERR_FD (ADR-054 §7). A trap that fires inside a call made
896	# with 2>/dev/null runs under that redirect, so the abort banner went to
897	# /dev/null when SIGTERM landed during one. A no-op when nothing was saved.
898	_runner_restore_stderr() {
899	    # Guard against a repeat signal (e.g. `timeout` forwarding its own SIGTERM
900	    # to the process group after the first already fired). Called only from
901	    # _runner_abort_trap (EXIT trap). Setting the guard here — as the very first
902	    # instruction inside the function body — closes the race window that exists
903	    # AFTER this function returns to _runner_abort_trap: bash checks pending
904	    # signals at function-return boundaries, so a pending second TERM would fire
905	    # _runner_signal_trap TERM (→ exit 1) before the explicit guard in
906	    # _runner_abort_trap could execute. By setting it HERE the guard is already
907	    # active by the time the function returns. B3 is satisfied because
908	    # _runner_restore_stderr is still the first call in _runner_abort_trap.
909	    # Ignored, not trapped with ':' (#2493): a handler run inside the trap broke
910	    # it off on bash 5.2, and a TERM to the group ended the trap's own command
911	    # substitutions, which take the default TERM.
912	    trap '' INT TERM
913	    [[ -n "${_RUNNER_ERR_FD:-}" ]] && exec 2>&"$_RUNNER_ERR_FD"
914	    return 0
915	}

917	_render_pipeline_end() {
918	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
919	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
920	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
921	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
922	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
923	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
924	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
925	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
926	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
927	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
928	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
929	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
930	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
931	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
932	    # (#1156)
933	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
934	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
935	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
936	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
937	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
938	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
939	
940	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
941	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
942	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
943	    local word
944	    case "$status" in
945	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
946	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
947	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
948	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
949	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
950	        timed_out)               word="timed_out" ;;
951	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
952	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
953	    esac
954	
955	    local label=" pipeline.end "
956	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
957	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
958	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
959	
960	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
961	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
962	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
963	
964	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
965	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
966	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
967	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
968	        local bar
969	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
970	        bar="${bar// /═}"
971	        {
972	            printf '\n'
973	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
974	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
975	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
976	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
977	        } >&2
978	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
979	        return 0
980	    fi
981	
982	    local lbar rbar
983	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
984	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
985	    {
986	        printf '\n'
987	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
988	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
989	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
990	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
991	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
992	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
993	    } >&2
994	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
995	}

997	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
998	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
999	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
1000	_runner_render_open_items() {
1001	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted|timed_out) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
1002	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1003	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n reason="${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}"

1005	    [[ "$1" == timed_out ]] && reason=timed_out

1008	    {
1009	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "$reason" "$n")"
1010	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1011	    } >&2

1014	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1015	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1016	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1017	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1018	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1019	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1020	#
1021	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1022	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1023	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1024	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1025	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1026	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1027	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1028	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1029	_render_stage_divider() {

content.content:
33	# resolve_stage_plugin <stage> [plugins_root]
34	# ADR-042: uniform stage→plugin resolution. Adopted by the cycle and parallel
35	# dispatch paths (runner.sh) to match the leaf path's pre-existing role-then-id
36	# rule (the leaf path keeps its own inline logic). A stage's flow-name need not
37	# equal its plugin `id` — role binding (ADR-001) is resolved FIRST, with id-match
38	# as the backward-compat fallback. Cycle and parallel members previously used
39	# id-only and so silently failed to resolve role-bound stages whose plugin id ≠
40	# stage name (e.g. lint→lint-gate, lens-*→review-lens).
41	# Single-plugin resolution (cycle/parallel members do NOT fan out): first match
42	# wins. Side-effect-free: echoes the plugin dir and returns 0 on hit, returns 1
43	# if nothing resolves. (The resolver's best-effort registry.role-unresolved
44	# diagnostic on a role miss is the same as every other strategy path.)
45	resolve_stage_plugin() {
46	    local stage="$1" plugins_root="${2:-${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-$_ZBUILD_DISPATCH_ROOT/plugins}}"
47	    local roles role platform plugin_dir
48	    # Role-then-id: try declared roles first (when template data + resolver present).
49	    if declare -F template_stage_roles >/dev/null 2>&1 && declare -F resolve_plugin_for_role >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	        roles="$(template_stage_roles "$stage" 2>/dev/null || true)"
51	        if [[ -n "$roles" ]]; then
52	            # Mirror fanout.sh ~41-43: platform-specific then generic. Use the
53	            # caller's detected platforms (dynamic scope from runner) when set;
54	            # the resolver itself falls back to generic plugins within one call.
55	            local -a _platforms=()
56	            if declare -p _DETECTED_PLATFORMS >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ ${#_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
57	                _platforms=("${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}")
58	            fi
59	            while IFS= read -r role; do
60	                [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
61	                for platform in "${_platforms[@]+"${_platforms[@]}"}"; do
62	                    plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
63	                    [[ -n "$plugin_dir" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
64	                done
65	                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
66	                [[ -n "$plugin_dir" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
67	            done <<< "$roles"
68	            # Fail-closed: roles were declared but none resolved — no id-match fallback.
69	            # Roles arrive newline-separated; substitute rather than word-split so a
70	            # role token containing a glob char cannot expand against the filesystem.
71	            printf 'resolve_stage_plugin: stage %s: unresolved declared roles: %s\n' \
72	                "$stage" "${roles//$'\n'/ }" >&2
73	            return 1
74	        fi
75	    fi
76	    # Fallback: backward-compat id match (stage name == manifest id).
77	    # Only reached when no roles are declared for this stage.
78	    plugin_dir="$(_find_plugin_for_stage "$stage" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
79	    [[ -n "$plugin_dir" ]] && { echo "$plugin_dir"; return 0; }
80	    return 1
81	}

# units — intake, design, build_test_cycle, review_lenses,
# pr — where build_test_cycle groups the build/test leaves plus the decomposed
# mechanical gate stages, and review_lenses is the advisory lens group.
#
# I10-A..C historically wrapped build/test/objective-gate in build_test_cycle.
# B6 (#1138, ADR-040 — amends ADR-013/ADR-021/ADR-019; executes ADR-037 §6) CUT
--
  - intake
  - delivery_loop
  - pr

# ─── always_run (#1831) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Stages that run on EVERY exit path — success, non-zero rc, SIGINT, SIGTERM,
--
# Each entry is an ordinary top-level stage section — resolved by `roles:` like
# any other stage, and bounded by its own `timeout_s:` (#1801). A name here with
# no section, or a section with no `roles:`, REFUSES the template rather than
# quietly running nothing.
always_run:
  - release

id: resume-minimal
name: Resume Minimal Pipeline
extends: simple
defaults:
  strategy: fanout

# Minimal 3-leaf roster (#1098, PC5): the resume-after-SIGINT contract
# (full-pipeline-sigint resume path, Wave 15-E #685) is NOT stage-count
# dependent — it needs only: a stage BEFORE build (intake) to prove resume
# skips an already-complete stage, the build stage that SIGINTs / re-runs,
# and a stage AFTER build (test) to prove resume continues past build.
# Replaces the full ~14-stage standard roster the test used to register so
# the two real subprocess runs (SIGINT + --resume) drive far fewer dispatch
# units. Linear flow, no cycles (resume logic is the same either way).
#
# #1270: this is a per-repo `.zbuild/templates/` overlay (extends: simple).
# When merged over the base, the resulting file carries BOTH the base `flow:`
# and this `stages:` list, so the loader treats it as OLD-shape and honors ONLY
# the stages below (the base roster is discarded — it just has to exist).
#
# Stages declare NO `roles:` block on purpose. With roles, the runner routes
# the stage through the fanout strategy (orch pool), which collapses a child
# rc=130 into a generic rc=1 — that would break the SIGINT-propagation
# contract (build returns 130 → runner must exit 130). Without roles, the
# runner resolves the plugin by stage ID and calls plugin_hook_call directly,
# preserving the leaf's exact rc (the same effective dispatch the standard
# template gets via cycle_dispatch_stage for its cycle-member build).
stages:
  - id: intake
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file, stdout]
      tail_lines: 200
  - id: build
    gate: auto
    io:
      destinations: [file, stdout]
      tail_lines: 200
    router:
      timeout_s: 900
      max_turns: 0
  - id: test
    gate: auto
    io:

    --arg run_id "frsh2-fresh-1805" \

# resume_mode). The stage.start=1 assertion above already covers the dispatch-side
# observable: if intake were skipped, intake_starts would not equal 1.
# DSFRSH-2 is a no-code requirement: must pass on current code; need not fail before.
_frsh2_stage_skips=0
if [[ -f "$_S_FRSH2_EVENTS_JSONL" ]]; then
    _frsh2_stage_skips="$(jq -r 'select(.type=="stage.skip") | .type' \
        "$_S_FRSH2_EVENTS_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
fi
assert_eq \
    "[#1805/DSFRSH-2] fresh run (no --resume) emits no stage.skip events (dispatch-unit skip guard does not activate for fresh runs)" \
    "0" "$_frsh2_stage_skips"

# read the persisted current_iter so the cycle restarts the interrupted
    # iteration. Consume the flag immediately so nested cycles and subsequent
    # re-entries always start at 1. On a fresh run or nested-loop re-entry,
    # always start at 1 so inner cycles reset correctly on each outer iteration.
    # _is_resume tracks whether THIS cycle entry is a resume (for DSCMBR-1 guard
    # below); it is NOT cleared by the flag consumption so the first-iter guard
    # can use it even after _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=false is consumed.
    local _start_iter
    local _is_resume=false
    if [[ "${_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
        _is_resume=true
        local _persisted_iter
        # Use jq --arg to pass cycle_id safely (matches the write path's --arg id,
        # so dots or other special chars in cycle_id resolve to the same key).
        _persisted_iter="$(jq -r --arg id "$cycle_id" \
            '.cycle_iterations[$id].current_iter // 0' \
            "$state_file" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
        [[ "$_persisted_iter" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || _persisted_iter=0
        # Consume the flag: nested cycles and subsequent re-entries start at 1.
        _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=false
        # Start at the persisted iter (re-run the interrupted iteration); fall
        # back to 1 when no iteration has been recorded yet.
        _start_iter=$(( _persisted_iter > 0 ? _persisted_iter : 1 ))
        # Red-team guard: a corrupt persisted iter > _CYCLE_MAX_ITER would cause
        # the loop to execute zero times and fall through to unconverged. Cap so
        # resume always runs at least one iteration (#1805).
        (( _CYCLE_MAX_ITER > 0 && _start_iter > _CYCLE_MAX_ITER )) \
            && _start_iter=$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER
    else
        _start_iter=1
    fi
    # DSFSTG-1 (#1805): when --from-stage targets this cycle, emit stage.start for
    # its first member even though _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE was cleared (iter always 1
    # for from-stage so persisted iter must not be used). Use a SEPARATE flag so
    # _is_resume stays false — the DSCMBR-1 skip guard must NOT run for from-stage
    # (it would skip members "complete" from prior runs, leaving no dispatches).
    # Consume the flag immediately so nested cycles and later iterations are not affected.
    local _from_stage_cycle_start=false
    if [[ "${_ZBUILD_FROM_STAGE_EMIT_START:-false}" == "true" ]]; then
        _from_stage_cycle_start=true
        export _ZBUILD_FROM_STAGE_EMIT_START=false
    fi

    _cycle_install_traps

    eb_emit_event "cycle.start" \
        "cycle_id=$cycle_id" "iter=$_start_iter" \
        "max=$_CYCLE_MAX_ITER" \
        "stages=${_CYCLE_STAGES[*]}" 2>/dev/null || true

    for (( iter=_start_iter; iter <= _CYCLE_MAX_ITER; iter++ )); do
        _CYCLE_TRAP_ITER="$iter"
        _CYCLE_LAST_ITERATIONS="$iter"

        # #682: 2 blank lines BEFORE each iter separator (inter-iter gap),
        # except before the very first iter where 1 blank is enough — the
        # divider function already prints its own leading `\n`, so emit ONE
        # extra blank here for iter>=2 (giving the operator a clear visual
        # break between iters distinct from within-iter stage gaps).
        if [[ "$iter" -ge 2 ]]; then

        # `cycle_iter_begin_hook` to call _render_cycle_iter_divider. Best-effort
        # (never aborts cycle on hook failure). Records wall clock for elapsed.

    # runs a generated standalone script (strategies/common.sh) the runner
    # cannot export into — but plugin_hook_call is its last line.

    # every reader spells `${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-<default>}`, and ADR-024 /
    # persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on it as a root. Derive from
    # ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR instead.

    # empty $1 keeps the ambient stage rather than blanking it. A caller with no
    # stage to name must not erase the one its own caller established — the

    # dispatch but read outside it (router-rc-classify.sh:154), so a blank here

    # cross-boundary reader and wants the literal argument.

# Returns:
#   0 — all succeeded
#   1 — all failed (collect failure with no successes)
#   2 — partial (at least one success, at least one fail); callers treat as stage fail
#   4 — no plugin found for any role (caller may fall back to stage-id lookup)
_strategy_run_fanout() {
    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): rc is 0 or 1; WHY rides this word, which the caller
    # reads in the same shell — ok | partial | empty | no_plugin | bad_dimension
    # | infra_failed | failed.
    _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="failed"
    local pool_id="$1" stage="$2" roles_out="$3" state_file="$4" plugins_root="$5"
    local success_count=0 fail_count=0 any_plugin_found=false dispatch_count=0
    local -a work_units=() dispatched_plugins=()

    local role platform plugin_dir wu
    while IFS= read -r role; do
        [[ -z "$role" ]] && continue
        for platform in "${_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]}"; do
            # Intentional fail-open: resolver returns "" when no match — skip silently.
            plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "$platform" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && \
                plugin_dir="$(resolve_plugin_for_role "$role" "" "$plugins_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            [[ -z "$plugin_dir" ]] && continue
            any_plugin_found=true

            wu="$(_strategy_make_work_unit "$plugin_dir" "$stage" "$state_file" "$platform")" || {
                warn "fanout: failed to create work unit for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            work_units+=("$wu")

            orch_dispatch "$pool_id" "$wu" >/dev/null || {
                warn "fanout: orch_dispatch failed for role=$role platform=$platform" || true
                fail_count=$((fail_count + 1))
                continue
            }
            dispatch_count=$((dispatch_count + 1))
            dispatched_plugins+=("$plugin_dir")
        done
    done <<< "$roles_out"

    if ! $any_plugin_found; then
        _strategy_cleanup_work_units "${work_units[@]+"${work_units[@]}"}"
        orch_shutdown "$pool_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        _ZB_STRATEGY_OUTCOME="no_plugin"
        return 1
    fi

    # Only collect if at least one dispatch succeeded; otherwise pool is empty
    # and orch_collect would return 0 (no results) — misreported as success.

scan_plugin_outputs() {
    local plugin_dir="$1"
    local state_file="${2:-}"
    local stage="${3:-}"
    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
    local probe="${4:-}"
    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"

    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0

    local plugin_id; yaml_get_v plugin_id "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true
    local kind; yaml_get_v kind "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true
    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
    local empty_diff_ok; yaml_get_v empty_diff_ok "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
        zb_dirname_v state_dir "$state_file"
        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
    fi

    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
    # support (per ADR-001):
    #   outputs:
    #     - name: foo
    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
    #       type: foo.json
    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
    local paths
    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"

    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0

    local missing=0
    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
        _registry_resolve_output_path_v resolved "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir"

        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
        _violation=""
        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
            _violation="absent"
            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
            _violation="empty"
            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
        fi

        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ -n "$_violation" ]]; then
            if [[ "$_violation" == "absent" ]]; then
                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output missing: $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
            else
                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output is empty (zero bytes): $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
            fi
            emit_event "$_event" \
                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                "kind=$kind" \
                "expected_path=$resolved" \
